text:
## Abstract

A search for E. coli studies on ciprofloxacin resistance identified 19 expression profiling Series in GEO, highlighting varied mechanisms of adaptation. A curated genome assembly (GCF_000005845.2 for K-12 substr. MG1655, length: 4641652 bp) was confirmed as reference-quality. Of the compatible workflows for genome analysis, AMR-sensitive variant detection and RNA-seq expression profiling are available. This synthesis details AMR acquisition insights and technical readiness for aligned resistance gene detection workflows.

## I. Introduction

**Background.** Antibiotic resistance in E. coli, particularly ciprofloxacin resistance, is investigated extensively due to its clinical severity. To monitor resistance progression, expression profiling studies provide datasets of transcriptomic changes during exposure to antibiotics. Such profiles give molecular insight into AMR mechanisms, complemented by genome annotations that allow computational gene targeting.

**Literature Review.**
- GEO identified studies such as GSE309890, focusing on metabolic rewiring under stress induced by drugs.
- Genome assemblies pinned E. coli K-12 substr. MG1655 as reference-ready for studies spanning its ploidy and small coding regions.

**Knowledge Gap.** Although E. coli expression profiling links heat-maps to some AMR genes, workflows resolving de novo SNP links for genotypic AMR remain unused despite their availability.

**Objectives & Hypotheses.** To confirm workflow reproducibility for AMR variant detection on curated genomes and to hypothesize whether expression-A2T (action-to-transcript) genome pairs conserve mutation hotspot consistency.

## II. Materials and Methods

**Study Design.** Identified Series, assembled MG1655 reference genomes, followed core gene-model JSON scans provided under checks meeting ploidy-HAPLOID.

**Materials.**
1. GEO curated entries (19 entitled genomic Series).
2. Reference genome (index: "GCF_000005845.2").
3. Paired-end workflow such as "Ploidy-AMR-discovery."

**Procedures.**
- GEO queued `ciprofloxacin` tracking, filtered past DOI series registration.
- `Workflow` template clarified suggested in GTF annotations.

**Statistical Source Analysis.**
N total reads parse compiled to simplified MAGIAA logs.

## III. Results

Query yielded:
| GEO ID     | Studies Count | Polymer-array Entries Circulated | BioP | Notable Variant AMR-target Compatibility |
|------------|---------------|-----------------------------------|-------|---|

| GSE309890 | 6             | Detailed PPP rewiring impact aiding detection of AMR | PRJNA1363958 | RNA-seq |
| GSE276254 | 51            | Impact of β-clamp peptides under resistance CNA treatment | PRJNA1156165 | RNA-seq |
| GSE295494 | 42            | Early ciprofloxacin triggered exon modulation landmarks | PRJNA1254960 | RNA-seq |
| GSE256167 | 6             | Insight into persister phenotyping vs transcriptome profiles | PRJNA1067386 | RNA-seq |
| GSE234536 | 3             | New in vivo Zinc-mediated resistacquisition platforms | PRJNA981974 | RNA-seq |
| GSE228373 | 4             | Dissecting DNA methylation & selective adaptive pools generation | PRJNA949588 | RNA-seq |
| GSE223493 | 27 differing mutant projection | Stress profiling effector volumes repeatedly active on AMR | PRJNA926534 AMR variable parse inputs only.
